chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Abu Ja'far, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Saif ibn 'Amirah, from Dawud ibn Farqad, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'All the districts/territories of the kings belong to the Imam, and the people have no share in them.'

key_terms.قَطَائِعُ: Districts or territories of land, specifically those owned by the ruler or state
key_terms.لِلْإِمَامِ: For the Imam (the divinely appointed leader)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the ownership of royal lands (qata'i') in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from the chapter on Anfal establishes the Imam's exclusive ownership of royal territories (qata'i'), a concept central to Shia political jurisprudence regarding state resources. It clarifies that these lands are not communal property but are reserved for the Imam's authority, distinguishing his governance from that of other rulers. This exclusivity underscores the Imam's role as the sole administrator of public wealth in the absence of the Prophet.
